parsed.explanation: Thin-data jurisdiction; extrapolating from structure. No provision criminalises trans identity as such, and no visitor-facing exposures (border screening, facility rules, detention placement) are documented. But the dossier shows police in one region arresting and torturing queer residents — an active enforcement lever that could be applied to gender-nonconforming people — plus an official ban on queer organising, a contested ten-year-sentence ordinance applied via public-morality provisions in the other region, no legal gender recognition, and very low documented social acceptance (130th). Trans-specific violence is mentioned but undated and uncounted; HIV care access is collapsing in one region. No documented protective machinery anywhere. This sits below the dead-letter-statute-plus-acceptance tier (0.55–0.65) but above pure societal-hostility cases, given documented state violence against the closest analogue community and an unresolved criminalisation question: around 0.42.
